findings.issue_text: Skipping the postgres test in module_server_test.go silences the test that exposed an init failure caused by moving Init into NewResourceServer, permanently losing postgres coverage and shipping the unreported init error

Removing the full-duration cacheMu lock from BuildIndex in bleve.go allows concurrent builds of the same index directory, causing the second bleve.New caller to fail with 'index already exists'-class errors due to lost serialization

Moving Init into NewResourceServer makes synchronous search index builds block construction, so callers relying on lazy init get a failed/nil server and every construction pays full index-build latency

The only integration test for the storage server's non-sqlite path is skipped with a TODO, leaving the lifecycle refactor (constructor-time Init) unverified with no tests asserting Init succeeds, initErr surfacing works, or RPCs work post-refactor on a real DB
Starting the watcher after the search index build in server.go:312 loses all writes occurring during the initial index build, producing a permanently stale index with no catch-up pass

The 'search index initialized' log in search.go:216 fires immediately after spawning the fire-and-forget indexing goroutine, logging duration_secs ~0 and a stale total_docs count that excludes the goroutine's work
Constructor-time Init in NewResourceServer converts degraded-per-request failure into total startup failure, with no verification that all call sites tolerate this contract change
The Init call uses the constructor's ctx, and the search-init goroutine inherits it, so a short-lived or request-scoped context will silently cancel background index building when it ends

Eager s.Init(ctx) in NewResourceServer converts a cheap constructor into a synchronous search-index build, changing the constructor's failure contract so a transient DB hiccup aborts construction/registration where RPCs previously lazily retried Init

Reordering initWatcher() to run after s.search.init(ctx) breaks the event-completeness invariant: writes committed between index-build snapshot and watcher registration produce no WrittenEvent, leaving the index permanently stale until full rebuild

Removing cacheMu from BuildIndex body allows two concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same NamespacedResource above FileThreshold to both call bleve.New on the same directory, causing the second build to fail
Concurrent duplicate in-memory index builds double the memory footprint transiently, contradicting the PR's performance goal
The b.cache[key] = idx last-writer-wins write discards the index other concurrent readers may already hold, orphaning bleve resources

Deleting the if err := s.Init(ctx) err guards from ten RPC entry points while retaining the lazy init machinery in Init leaves two parallel initialization paths; callers bypassing NewResourceServer now hit nil-pointer failures (e.g., History calling s.search.History with no nil check) instead of explicit initErr

New Info-level log line 'search index initialized' with duration_secs/total_docs fires unconditionally on every server start, adding log noise and requiring TotalDocs as public API, duplicating the existing IndexMetrics.IndexCreationTime metric

The postgres t.Skip in module_server_test.go removes the only integration coverage of the eager-init path on a production database backend, with a TODO instead of a tracked issue or fix, merging an unfixed environmental failure
Reordering initWatcher() to run after search.init creates an unwatched gap where writes between index snapshot and watcher startup are permanently missing from the search index
Moving Init into NewResourceServer makes search/index construction a hard startup dependency, so transient backend failures at boot take down the whole server with no retry path
Removing every handler's Init(ctx) call leaves servers constructed outside NewResourceServer (test fixtures, embeds, secondary constructors) operating on an uninitialized watcher/index with no guard
Dropping the whole-method cacheMu lock in BuildIndex allows concurrent duplicate bleve builds for the same key, including concurrent bleve.New on the same on-disk directory causing corruption
The only integration test for the instrumentation server target is skipped for postgres, leaving the primary production database path untested in CI
Remaining lazy Init callers with request-scoped contexts would cancel the long-running index build mid-build, leaving a half-built cached index

Reordering initWatcher() to run after s.search.init(ctx) in pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go silently drops write events during index build, causing in-memory index to serve stale results until restart
Moving s.Init(ctx) from RPC methods into NewResourceServer changes failure contract from lazy per-request errors to fatal constructor failure, with removed Init call sites untested
t.Skip in pkg/server/module_server_test.go disables the only postgres CI coverage for the storage server init subsystem this PR changes
Narrowing cacheMu scope in bleve.go allows concurrent duplicate index builds for the same key, causing metric inflation and event handling on a shadow index
benign last-writer-wins race on duplicate index builds in bleve.go due to cache lock moved to only the final b.cache[key] = idx write

Postgres t.Skip in module_server_test.go disables the only integration test covering the construct-and-serve path, converting a failing (red) test into a green suite and giving false confidence in the eager-Init behavior

The eager-Init + reordered init sequence (search.init before initWatcher) in NewResourceServer is validated on only one database backend due to skips, and the skip comment suggests the new init path is actually broken
No test exercises NewResourceServer returning an error, the new s.search.init(ctx) with propagated context, or the watcher-after-index ordering

Narrowing cacheMu to only the cache write in bleve.go allows two concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same key to both run the full build, with the second overwriting the first index handle, causing readers holding the first index to diverge from the cache's canonical index
No test exercises concurrent BuildIndex behavior after the lock-scope narrowing in bleve.go
The removed 'if err == nil { b.log.Info(...) }' block was replaced with an unconditional TODO comment, indicating the code is mid-refactor and not known-equivalent

Init reordering: search.init now runs before initWatcher, so writes occurring during the potentially long index build are never captured by the watcher, leaving the search index permanently stale (deleted dashboards still appear, new ones missing) with no backfill or reconciliation

Moving s.Init(ctx) into NewResourceServer makes a transient init failure unrecoverable: the constructor returns nil, err and the server never starts, whereas previously lazy per-request init allowed retries and self-healing
Init now runs the full search-index build synchronously inside the constructor, blocking NewResourceServer callers for the entire build duration
Removing cacheMu lock around BuildIndex allows two concurrent getOrCreateIndex calls for the same key to each run a full index build, doubling DB load
Without cacheMu, concurrent file-backed index builds can both attempt bleve.New on the same directory, causing the loser to return a spurious already-open-directory error to the caller

Background indexing failure is now permanently invisible: Init returns nil while index build is still in flight, and deleted per-request initErr checks mean no code path ever observes initErr, so the server reports healthy and serves empty/partial results

Constructor's ctx flows into the fire-and-forget index-build goroutine, so the long-running build runs under an already-cancelled/ended context (span's ctx), causing DB iteration to abort mid-build with no error surfaced

Removing the cacheMu hold across BuildIndex opens a concurrent-build race: two bleve indexes can be constructed for the same file-backed directory concurrently, and the loser's cache write is discarded, orphaning a fully-built index (leak)
The 'search index initialized' log line is emitted immediately after spawning the background goroutine, so duration_secs and total_docs report incorrect values (~0 duration, unpopulated doc count)

goldens.comment: A race condition in BuildIndex allows multiple goroutines to concurrently build the same expensive index for the same key. This is caused by moving the b.cacheMu lock from protecting the entire function to only protecting the final cache assignment.

Calling s.search.TotalDocs() here may race with concurrent index creation: TotalDocs iterates b.cache without synchronization, and the event watcher goroutine started just above could trigger BuildIndex writes concurrently, potentially causing a concurrent map read/write panic.

per_golden_matches.golden_comment: A race condition in BuildIndex allows multiple goroutines to concurrently build the same expensive index for the same key. This is caused by moving the b.cacheMu lock from protecting the entire function to only protecting the final cache assignment.

per_golden_matches.reasoning: Both describe the same underlying concurrency bug: narrowing/removing the full-duration cacheMu lock in BuildIndex loses serialization, allowing multiple goroutines to concurrently build the same index for the same key/directory (wasting work and potentially causing 'already exists' failures).

per_golden_matches.golden_comment: Calling s.search.TotalDocs() here may race with concurrent index creation: TotalDocs iterates b.cache without synchronization, and the event watcher goroutine started just above could trigger BuildIndex writes concurrently, potentially causing a concurrent map read/write panic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Skipping the postgres test in module_server_test.go silences the test that exposed an init failure caused by moving Init into NewResourceServer, permanently losing postgres coverage and shipping the unreported init error

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds a `t.Skip` for `dbType == "postgres"` in `module_server_test.go`, which reduces/loses postgres coverage for that integration test. Separately, `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` and request handlers no longer call `Init`, so failures that would previously surface during RPC calls can now surface at construction time. However, the claim that this will "ship the unreported init error" isn’t supported by the diff: `NewResourceServer` logs and returns the init error (`return nil, err`), so it would be reported rather than silently shipped. The review concern is mainly about masking postgres-specific regressions by skipping the test, not a proven runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removing the full-duration cacheMu lock from BuildIndex in bleve.go allows concurrent builds of the same index directory, causing the second bleve.New caller to fail with 'index already exists'-class errors due to lost serialization
matched_golden_ids: A race condition in BuildIndex allows multiple goroutines to concurrently build the same expensive index for the same key. This is caused by moving the b.cacheMu lock from protecting the entire function to only protecting the final cache assignment.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same underlying concurrency bug: narrowing/removing the full-duration cacheMu lock in BuildIndex loses serialization, allowing multiple goroutines to concurrently build the same index for the same key/directory (wasting work and potentially causing 'already exists' failures).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Moving Init into NewResourceServer makes synchronous search index builds block construction, so callers relying on lazy init get a failed/nil server and every construction pays full index-build latency

adjudication.rationale: The diff does move initialization from per-RPC lazy calls into constructor time: `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` and returns `nil, err` on failure, while all the `if err := s.Init(ctx); err != nil { ... }` checks were removed from `Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/...` (server.go). `Init` includes `s.search.init(ctx)` (which can build/initialize the index) and `s.initWatcher()`, so construction can now synchronously pay that latency and can fail the constructor rather than deferring failure to first use. Whether this is a “bug” depends on intended API/behavior, which isn’t verifiable from the diff alone, but the review concern is real and specific to these changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The only integration test for the storage server's non-sqlite path is skipped with a TODO, leaving the lifecycle refactor (constructor-time Init) unverified with no tests asserting Init succeeds, initErr surfacing works, or RPCs work post-refactor on a real DB

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds a TODO and skips the integration test when `dbType == "postgres"` in `TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer` (`module_server_test.go`), reducing CI coverage for the non-sqlite path. At the same time, `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` and all the per-RPC `s.Init(ctx)` calls are removed (`pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go`), which is a nontrivial lifecycle change that would benefit from integration coverage on a real DB to ensure Init errors surface and RPCs still work after constructor-time Init. The claim that this is the *only* such integration test isn’t verifiable from the diff alone, but the skip + refactor gap is diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Starting the watcher after the search index build in server.go:312 loses all writes occurring during the initial index build, producing a permanently stale index with no catch-up pass

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly reorders initialization in `server.Init`: it now calls `s.search.init(ctx)` before starting the watcher (`s.initWatcher()`), whereas previously the watcher started first. That ordering change could plausibly allow resource writes/updates occurring during the potentially long `search.init` index build window to be missed by the watcher, depending on whether `initWatcher()` can replay/catch up from a known resource version. However, the diff does not show `initWatcher()`’s implementation or any explicit catch-up mechanism, so the claim that it *definitely* “loses all writes” and results in a “permanently stale index” is not fully verifiable from the provided changes alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The 'search index initialized' log in search.go:216 fires immediately after spawning the fire-and-forget indexing goroutine, logging duration_secs ~0 and a stale total_docs count that excludes the goroutine's work

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a new log line `s.log.Info("search index initialized", ...)` added after `end := time.Now().Unix()` in `searchSupport.init()`, but it does not show that the main index build work is done in a “fire-and-forget” goroutine. The only visible clue is an anonymous function invocation ending with `}()`, but the diff snippet does not include whether it is prefixed with `go` nor what work it performs. Without that context, the claim that the log will always report ~0 duration and a stale `TotalDocs()` (excluding goroutine work) is not verifiable from the provided diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Constructor-time Init in NewResourceServer converts degraded-per-request failure into total startup failure, with no verification that all call sites tolerate this contract change

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes initialization semantics: `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` and returns an error on failure (pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go), while multiple RPC handlers remove their per-call `s.Init(ctx)` checks (Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/History/Origin/IsHealthy/PutBlob/GetBlob). This converts a previously lazy/per-request init failure mode into a constructor-time hard failure. Whether that is a defect depends on external call-site expectations (not shown in the diff), but the contract change is real and review-relevant.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The Init call uses the constructor's ctx, and the search-init goroutine inherits it, so a short-lived or request-scoped context will silently cancel background index building when it ends

adjudication.rationale: The diff moves initialization to the constructor path: `NewResourceServer` now calls `err := s.Init(ctx)` and request handlers no longer call `Init(ctx)`. In `searchSupport.init(ctx)`, the span start was changed to `ctx, span := ...`, and the function launches a goroutine (`go func() { ... }()`) that will capture and use the `ctx` from `init`. This means whatever `ctx` is passed into `NewResourceServer`/`Init` will be inherited by background index-building work; if that constructor `ctx` can be short-lived/cancelled, it can prematurely cancel that goroutine. The diff doesn’t show where `ctx` in `NewResourceServer` originates, so it’s a grounded concern but not a provable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Eager s.Init(ctx) in NewResourceServer converts a cheap constructor into a synchronous search-index build, changing the constructor's failure contract so a transient DB hiccup aborts construction/registration where RPCs previously lazily retried Init

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes initialization from per-RPC lazy calls to eager construction-time init: `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` and returns an error if init fails (server.go +255), while all the `if err := s.Init(ctx); err != nil { ... }` guards were removed from RPC handlers (Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/etc.). Since `Init` can run `s.search.init(ctx)` (which builds/loads the search index) and `s.initWatcher()`, this does make the constructor potentially synchronous/expensive and changes when errors surface (construction/registration time vs first RPC). However, the finding’s claim that RPCs "previously lazily retried Init" is not supported by the diff: `Init` uses `s.initOnce.Do(...)` and stores `s.initErr`, so a transient failure would not be retried on later RPCs anyway. The concern about constructor cost/contract is real, but not a verifiable defect on its own.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Reordering initWatcher() to run after s.search.init(ctx) breaks the event-completeness invariant: writes committed between index-build snapshot and watcher registration produce no WrittenEvent, leaving the index permanently stale until full rebuild

adjudication.rationale: The diff does reorder initialization in `(*server).Init`: it now calls `s.search.init(ctx)` before `s.initWatcher()` (see `pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go`). If `search.init` builds the index from a point-in-time snapshot while the watcher only delivers events from the time it is registered (no catch-up), writes occurring during `search.init` could be missed and leave the index stale. However, the diff does not show how `initWatcher()` works (e.g., whether it can resume from a revision/offset), so the claimed invariant break cannot be conclusively verified from the provided changes alone; it’s a concrete, diff-grounded race concern rather than a proven bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removing cacheMu from BuildIndex body allows two concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same NamespacedResource above FileThreshold to both call bleve.New on the same directory, causing the second build to fail

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go, BuildIndex previously held b.cacheMu for the entire function (including the bleve.New(dir, mapper) call). The diff removes that outer lock and now only locks around `b.cache[key] = idx`. With this change, two goroutines can concurrently enter BuildIndex for the same `key` and `size > FileThreshold`, both compute the same `dir` and both call `bleve.New(dir, mapper)` concurrently. Since `bleve.New` creates a new index at that path, the second call can fail due to the directory/index already being created by the first. The diff provides no other synchronization to prevent this scenario.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Concurrent duplicate in-memory index builds double the memory footprint transiently, contradicting the PR's performance goal

adjudication.rationale: In `pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go`, `BuildIndex` previously held `b.cacheMu` for the entire build (`Lock`/`defer Unlock`), but the diff removes that and now only locks around `b.cache[key] = idx`. This change makes it possible for concurrent calls to `BuildIndex` for the same `key` to build separate Bleve indexes (including `bleve.NewMemOnly`) before either one is stored in the cache, temporarily duplicating memory usage and potentially wasting work. The diff does not show any other per-key singleflight/guard that would prevent this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The b.cache[key] = idx last-writer-wins write discards the index other concurrent readers may already hold, orphaning bleve resources

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go, BuildIndex previously held cacheMu for the entire function (including index creation) but now only locks around `b.cache[key] = idx`. This allows concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same `key` to race and both build/open separate bleve indexes, with the last write overwriting the cached entry. While the finding’s claim about “discarding the index other concurrent readers already hold” isn’t directly shown (a reader holding the returned `idx` still has it), the diff does introduce a real last-writer-wins caching/concurrency concern and potential extra/unused index instances depending on how cleanup/Close is handled elsewhere (not shown in the diff).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Deleting the if err := s.Init(ctx) err guards from ten RPC entry points while retaining the lazy init machinery in Init leaves two parallel initialization paths; callers bypassing NewResourceServer now hit nil-pointer failures (e.g., History calling s.search.History with no nil check) instead of explicit initErr

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows RPC methods no longer call `s.Init(ctx)`, but `NewResourceServer` now eagerly calls `s.Init(ctx)` and returns an error on failure. The finding’s claim about “two parallel initialization paths” and “callers bypassing `NewResourceServer`” is speculative—there’s no evidence in the diff that the server is constructed other than via `NewResourceServer`. Also, the cited example (`History` calling `s.search.History` with no nil check) would have panicked even before this change: previously `History` called `Init` but `Init` does not ensure `s.search` is non-nil (it only initializes it if already non-nil), so a nil `s.search` would still lead to a nil-pointer dereference after `Init` returned nil.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New Info-level log line 'search index initialized' with duration_secs/total_docs fires unconditionally on every server start, adding log noise and requiring TotalDocs as public API, duplicating the existing IndexMetrics.IndexCreationTime metric

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go, searchSupport.init now always emits an Info log line `s.log.Info("search index initialized", "duration_secs", end-start, "total_docs", s.search.TotalDocs())` after initialization, regardless of log level configuration beyond Info. This is a diff-grounded change that can increase startup log volume and is arguably redundant with the existing IndexMetrics.IndexCreationTime observation done immediately after. The part about "requiring TotalDocs as public API" is not verifiable from the diff alone (TotalDocs already exists and we can't see whether its visibility changed), but the unconditional Info log/noise and duplication with metrics is a concrete review concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The postgres t.Skip in module_server_test.go removes the only integration coverage of the eager-init path on a production database backend, with a TODO instead of a tracked issue or fix, merging an unfixed environmental failure

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new conditional skip for `dbType == "postgres"` in `TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer` with a TODO note (`t.Skip("skipping - test not working with postgres in Drone. Works locally.")`). This is a concrete, diff-grounded reduction in CI coverage for Postgres due to an acknowledged environmental failure, without a tracked issue/fix. However, the claim that it removes the *only* integration coverage of the eager-init path on a production DB backend is not verifiable from this diff alone (the test name/contents shown don’t establish that).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Reordering initWatcher() to run after search.init creates an unwatched gap where writes between index snapshot and watcher startup are permanently missing from the search index

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go, Init() was changed to run s.search.init(ctx) before s.initWatcher() (previously watcher started first). search.init() appears to build an initial index snapshot (it measures creation time and logs total docs), while ongoing updates are handled via events (handleEvent(evt *WrittenEvent)). If writes can occur concurrently during initialization (e.g., from other nodes/processes sharing the same backend), starting the watcher only after the snapshot build creates a window where those writes are neither in the snapshot nor observed by the watcher, leaving the search index permanently missing them.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Moving Init into NewResourceServer makes search/index construction a hard startup dependency, so transient backend failures at boot take down the whole server with no retry path

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `err := s.Init(ctx)` inside `NewResourceServer` and returns an error on failure (`return nil, err`). Previously, `Init` was invoked lazily at the start of many RPC handlers (Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/etc.), allowing the server object to be constructed even if initialization would fail at that moment. With this change, search initialization (`s.search.init(ctx)`) and watcher startup run during construction and will prevent the server from starting if they fail. While the “no retry path” aspect isn’t newly introduced (Init uses `s.initOnce.Do`, so a failure is sticky either way), making init a constructor-time dependency does turn transient backend/search/index issues at boot into a hard startup failure rather than a deferred (first-request) failure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removing every handler's Init(ctx) call leaves servers constructed outside NewResourceServer (test fixtures, embeds, secondary constructors) operating on an uninitialized watcher/index with no guard

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the per-RPC `s.Init(ctx)` guard from many handlers (Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/History/Origin/IsHealthy/PutBlob/GetBlob) and instead calls `s.Init(ctx)` only inside `NewResourceServer` (new block added around line ~255). This is a behavior change: if a `*server` instance is created by any path other than `NewResourceServer` (e.g., in-package tests or alternative constructors), calls into these handlers would no longer auto-initialize the watcher/search index, and could operate with `initWatcher`/`search.init` never run. The diff itself doesn’t prove such alternative construction exists, so it’s a valid architectural/risk concern but not a verifiable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dropping the whole-method cacheMu lock in BuildIndex allows concurrent duplicate bleve builds for the same key, including concurrent bleve.New on the same on-disk directory causing corruption

adjudication.rationale: In `pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go` `BuildIndex`, the diff removes the `b.cacheMu.Lock()`/`defer Unlock()` that previously serialized the entire method. Now the mutex only guards `b.cache[key] = idx`, while the expensive build/open path (including `bleve.New(dir, mapper)` for on-disk indexes) runs unlocked. The diff shows the directory is deterministically derived from `key` (`filepath.Join(b.opts.Root, key.Namespace, fmt.Sprintf("%s.%s", ...))`), so concurrent calls for the same `key` can both attempt `bleve.New` on the same on-disk directory before either stores to the cache, leading to duplicate builds and potential on-disk index corruption / undefined behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The only integration test for the instrumentation server target is skipped for postgres, leaving the primary production database path untested in CI

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/server/module_server_test.go, the integration test TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer now explicitly skips when dbType == "postgres" with a TODO comment noting it fails in Drone CI. This reduces CI coverage for the postgres path (likely the main production DB) for this instrumentation-server-target integration test, leaving it untested in CI as stated.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Remaining lazy Init callers with request-scoped contexts would cancel the long-running index build mid-build, leaving a half-built cached index

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the per-request lazy initialization calls (`s.Init(ctx)`) from all RPC handlers (Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/History/Origin/IsHealthy/PutBlob/GetBlob). Initialization is instead performed eagerly in `NewResourceServer` via `err := s.Init(ctx)` before returning the server. Therefore the stated issue about “remaining lazy Init callers with request-scoped contexts” canceling a long-running build is not supported by this diff; those lazy callers were explicitly deleted here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Reordering initWatcher() to run after s.search.init(ctx) in pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go silently drops write events during index build, causing in-memory index to serve stale results until restart

adjudication.rationale: The diff does reorder initialization in `server.Init`: `s.search.init(ctx)` now runs before `s.initWatcher()` (previously watcher started first). If the watcher is responsible for consuming write events to keep the search index up to date, this reordering could allow writes occurring during `search.init` (index build) to go unobserved unless `search.init`/`initWatcher` explicitly backfills from a known version. However, the diff does not show `initWatcher()` behavior (e.g., whether it starts from a stored RV or “now”), nor whether `search.init` accounts for concurrent writes, so the claim of “silently drops write events … stale until restart” cannot be verified from the provided changes alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Moving s.Init(ctx) from RPC methods into NewResourceServer changes failure contract from lazy per-request errors to fatal constructor failure, with removed Init call sites untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly moves initialization to construction: `NewResourceServer` now calls `err := s.Init(ctx)` and returns an error on failure, while all per-RPC `if err := s.Init(ctx); err != nil { ... }` call sites are removed from `Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/History/Origin/IsHealthy/PutBlob/GetBlob`. That is a concrete change from lazy, per-request init failures to eager constructor failure, affecting callers’ error/availability behavior. The finding’s point about removed call sites being untested is plausible from the diff (no accompanying tests shown for the new contract), but the diff alone doesn’t prove missing tests beyond this PR snippet.

adjudication_records.issue_text: t.Skip in pkg/server/module_server_test.go disables the only postgres CI coverage for the storage server init subsystem this PR changes

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new conditional `t.Skip` when `dbType == "postgres"` in `pkg/server/module_server_test.go`, explicitly disabling this integration test for Postgres in CI (“test not working with postgres in Drone”). This is a concrete reduction in Postgres test coverage in the same PR that changes storage server initialization behavior (e.g., `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` and per-RPC `Init` calls were removed). However, the claim that this was the *only* Postgres CI coverage for the init subsystem is not verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Narrowing cacheMu scope in bleve.go allows concurrent duplicate index builds for the same key, causing metric inflation and event handling on a shadow index

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go, BuildIndex previously held b.cacheMu for the entire method (including index creation and builder execution). The diff removes that wide lock and only locks around `b.cache[key] = idx`. This change allows two goroutines to concurrently execute BuildIndex for the same `key`, both creating/building separate bleve indexes and both incrementing `resource.IndexMetrics.IndexTenants...Inc()` before either updates the cache. The last writer wins in `b.cache`, while the other caller still receives and may use a different (now “shadow”) index instance; metrics can also be inflated due to duplicate increments.

adjudication_records.issue_text: benign last-writer-wins race on duplicate index builds in bleve.go due to cache lock moved to only the final b.cache[key] = idx write

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go, BuildIndex previously held b.cacheMu for the entire method, preventing concurrent builds from running at once. The diff removes that full-method lock and only locks around `b.cache[key] = idx` at the end. From the diff alone, that permits concurrent goroutines to build an index for the same `key` simultaneously, and whichever finishes last will overwrite the cache entry (last-writer-wins). adjudication_records.issue_text: Removing the cacheMu hold across BuildIndex opens a concurrent-build race: two bleve indexes can be constructed for the same file-backed directory concurrently, and the loser's cache write is discarded, orphaning a fully-built index (leak)

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go, BuildIndex no longer holds b.cacheMu for the duration of the build (the initial Lock/Unlock was removed), and now only locks around `b.cache[key] = idx`. Only the last one to acquire the lock will be retained in `b.cache`, discarding the other built index object; for file-backed indexes this also risks concurrent creation/use of the same directory path (`dir := filepath.Join(...)`) and orphaning resources from the losing build. The diff provides no other synchronization preventing concurrent builds for the same key.
